v1.kill_reason: No strong reference can be obtained. The seed's base version (v1.13.2) contradicts the PR's 2019 merge date. The identifiable change covers partition and broadcast, not zip/flatten/product. No measured speedup exists, so the 2^u-1 normalisation has no pinned ceiling. Separately, the partition-view approach is public and recallable (K8/K11 risk) if re-scoped.

spike_plan.kill_if: The pre-change tree does not build, no measurable gain exists, or zip/flatten/product have no upstream change to use as a reference.
spike_plan.pass_if: Both builds succeed, the partition gain is measurable (at least 1.5x on a hidden-style workload), and at least two other iterator levers show a real upstream change to reference.
steps: In a throwaway networked Linux container, clone JuliaLang/julia and check out 3f0e7d6^ (the pre-change commit) and 3f0e7d6 separately; confirm v1.13.2 is not the base of the change.
Build both trees with make -j8 (expect 30-60 min each) and record build success or failure.
Run a micro-benchmark of Iterators.partition over arrays, plus zip, flatten and product, on both builds; record medians over 5 runs.
Diff base/iterators.jl between 3f0e7d6^ and current master to see whether zip/flatten/product changed; if not, drop those levers from the scope.
Check determinism: repeat the timing 3 times and compare spread.

v1.summary: The seed's source is real (Julia PR #33533, MIT), but the stated base v1.13.2 contradicts the PR's November 2019 merge, and the PR does not cover zip, flatten or product. No measured speedup or pinned reference exists, so the seed is killed as K5. It could be revived only after the reference is redefined to a specific pinned commit with a measured speedup, and the recallable upstream approach is accounted for.
